label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Mr. Bergeron, you’re right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid for bread in advance. I should have given you one before putting a mysterious sign in the window. This is Hélène, from Le Pétrin Doré, and I have good news, although this is not quite how I imagined sharing it.

We are not closing or moving. The building was sold—to me! We signed at the notary on December 15. After opening the bakery in March 2009 and spending nearly 17 years on this corner, I have bought the building. I wanted to keep the news as a surprise for the reopening, but I can see now that I left too much room for people to worry.

First, about the carnets, because I don’t want anyone to have to read a whole long message to find out what happens to their money: **every carnet is still valid. There is no expiry date.** You paid $60 for 12 loaves, and we will honour every loaf you have left. We sold 214 carnets in October, and the January closure changes nothing about that commitment.

To noodle_and_crumb: your seven loaves are still yours. You can use your carnet before the work starts or after we reopen, and you do not have to rush to finish it in January. That goes for everyone. Each carnet holder is also welcome to one free croissant in January, as a thank-you.

And if anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me. I will refund what remains on your carnet, no questions asked. You don’t need to explain yourself or feel uncomfortable asking.

I do want to say one thing honestly: reading the word “scam” hurt. I’ve spent nearly 17 years baking here, getting to know your families and seeing children grow up into people who now come in for their own coffee and bread. These carnets were not a way to collect money and disappear. They are a promise of bread, and I intend to keep it.

But I also understand that you cannot know what I haven’t told you. You saw a vague sign, heard that the building had sold, and wondered what would happen next. I should have been clearer. That part is my responsibility.

Here are the dates, without any more suspense: **we will be closed January 4 through January 18, and we reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

This is a closure for work in the bakery. We are getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. I have a certain affection for it after all these years, but I will be very happy to have its replacement.

We are also taking over the space at the back that used to be the dépanneur’s storage area. There will be six small tables. Not a huge dining room, just somewhere you can finally sit down, have your coffee and enjoy something from the bakery without having to carry it away. I have wanted that for a long time, and I’m very happy it is happening.

For the neighbours wondering about the three apartments upstairs: **the same tenants are staying, at the same rent.** I have given them that promise in writing. To our upstairs tenants, I want to say it here too, so you aren’t left answering rumours about your own homes. Buying the building does not mean I am pushing you out. The bakery is staying, and so are you.

Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right! The building really was sold. But there are no condos, bank or vape shop coming in place of Le Pétrin Doré.

M. Ferland, who owned the building, is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell it to me before anyone else. He has been coming in every morning for his baguette, “pas trop cuite,” for 17 years. At the notary, he cried a little. This was not just paperwork for him, and it was not just paperwork for me either. I’m grateful that he gave me the chance to keep the bakery here.

As for the famous sign: my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking enough about how it would look from the other side of the window. I am not blaming Thomas. I approved it! In my head, it meant a new oven, a place to sit, and finally owning our building. Of course, nobody walking past could read all that into those two words.

The half-empty shelves on the 28th were not a sign that we were winding down, either. We had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches. It was Christmas, not a closing sale.

Priya, thank you for what you wrote, and thank you to everyone who spoke up for us or worried about losing the bakery. I know Mile End has lost many small shops. When another window gets a sign, people fear the worst. I understand that, even if it was difficult to read some of the guesses about us.

So please come celebrate with us on **Saturday, January 23**. We will already be back baking from Tuesday the 19th at 7 a.m., but Saturday is our chance to welcome everyone for the reopening celebration. There will be free coffee and a piece of the new bread. Come see the changes, try the bread, and say hello—whether you defended us, worried about us, or simply want to know what is going on at your neighbourhood bakery.

I wish I had told you all this sooner. I was saving a happy surprise, and instead I gave you a reason to worry. I hope you can be happy with me now. This is a big moment for me, and I’m glad I get to share it with the neighbourhood that has kept us baking since 2009.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
